A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same samplers and theoretical framework, with the same title and authors. The main text, equations, comparison table, and complete Appendices A–I support comparison despite substantial proof revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports convergence theorems and mathematical proofs. Table 1 compares analytical guarantees; neither the main text nor appendices report original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: V2 likewise contains theoretical guarantees and proof appendices, without original experiments, simulations, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: The score-based reverse mean, Hessian-corrected Gaussian covariance, Hessian-matching objective, and early-stopping schedule are retained. V1 Section 5.1 matches v2 Sections 5.1–5.2; the changed guarantees do not establish a changed sampling algorithm.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts training or evaluation experiments. The revised coverage of distribution classes concerns mathematical guarantees, not empirically tested tasks.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates experimental baselines. V2's additional D-SDE and accelerated-DT comparisons in Table 1 concern cited analytical bounds.

E3.justification: No experimental protocols, splits, training budgets, or evaluation procedures are reported in either version. The noise-schedule formula and KL, total-variation, and Wasserstein distance framework remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither PDF reports ablations, empirical robustness tests, or supplementary experimental analyses. The appendix revisions concern mathematical error bounds and proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Score and Hessian estimation-error assumptions are theoretical conditions, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The analytical result entries change substantially: Theorems 4 and 8 replace leading KL-bound factors δ^-2 and δ^-3 with log^2(1/δ) and log^3(1/δ), under revised target assumptions. V1's additional linear-in-dimension special-case bound disappears. Gaussian-mixture rates in Theorems 3 and 7 remain unchanged, although v2 Table 1 omits their mixture-component factors. These are analytical changes, not measured performance gains.

T1.justification: Assumption 4 replaces derivative envelopes and summability requirements with moment conditions at Xt and the reverse mean. Jensen's inequality simplifies Appendices A and G, removes Theorem 1's extra trace term, and eliminates auxiliary mismatch conditions from Theorem 5; Theorem 6 drops score Lipschitzness. New derivative-moment and change-of-measure arguments support the revised early-stopping theorems. Assumption 1 also strengthens the dimension-uniform requirement from a second-moment matrix bound to E||X0||² <= M2. V1's general accelerated Corollary 3 is retained as v2 Corollary 2 in Appendix H.3.

C1.justification: The central convergence-and-acceleration contribution remains, but the headline explicit-parameter guarantees expand from bounded-support targets to finite-second-moment targets with early stopping and sharper δ dependence. Acceleration is now advertised under Lipschitz Hessians without the former score-Lipschitz requirement. The introduction drops the separate claim that handling estimation error distinguishes the work from prior acceleration.

C2.justification: New Section 1.2 discusses dimension-versus-accuracy tradeoffs against D-SDE guarantees and explains the different parameterizations. The conclusion changes the remaining challenge from improving δ dependence to improving dimension dependence. V1's detailed practical interpretation contrasting its covariance estimator with the prior accelerated sampler is removed.

D1.justification: Neither version provides code or data access, hardware, measured runtime, or an implemented training configuration. The documented Hessian-matching procedure is retained; revised estimator-error conditions are mathematical assumptions.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning through a dedicated DT-versus-D-SDE comparison section and an expanded Table 1. It adds Li et al.'s accelerated diffusion work and newer references on probability-flow ODEs, flow matching, Gaussian-mixture learning, and score estimation. Existing references updated from preprints to publications are retained works, not new additions.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around DT and D-SDE terminology. A comparison section is inserted, related work is reorganized, Hessian matching receives its own subsection, and proof exposition is substantially condensed and restructured. The general accelerated corollary moves from the main text to Appendix H.3.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a sampler column, separate D-SDE/regular-DT/accelerated-DT groups, additional rows, and blue highlighting for this paper's results. Author affiliations and some equation layouts also change. The overall single-column format remains, with no figures added.

improvement.justification: The revised derivations in Appendices E, F, and H address v1's explicitly unresolved polynomial δ dependence and provide explicit guarantees for unbounded finite-moment targets. The direct Jensen argument also simplifies the central proofs and removes auxiliary conditions. These are substantial theoretical and explanatory gains. Drawbacks include the stronger dimension-uniform moment assumption, removal of the special linear-d bound, and inconsistent summaries: v2's text after Theorem 1 states O(ε^-1) steps despite its T^-1 KL bound, while Table 1 suppresses mixture-component factors. These limit, but do not outweigh, the improvements.
